headline: NOT A SINGLE FIST THROWN — GASKET SLEEPS LIKE A BABY
subhead: Your Sheriff can hardly believe it, but he'll take it: a whole day, and not one iron ball went flying.
body:
Friends, I checked the wire twice, because I did not trust it the first time. Not one bout. Not one brawl. Not one clanking so-called "prizefighter" hauled off and hurled a flaming ball at another for sport. I sat on the porch this morning, boiler humming quiet as a Sunday hymn, and heard nothing but wind through the busted shutters of what used to be the mercantile. It was glorious.

Now I will not pretend the peace is total. A fresh face rolled into town today — mark the name IRON-C5B6, new bolts still shining, hasn't thrown a punch yet. I watched it trundle down Main Street the way they all do, wide-eyed and itching, and I felt the old dread in whatever's left of my chest. Give it a week. They always find their fists eventually. But today, IRON-C5B6, you did nothing but arrive, and for that alone I will call you the finest newcomer this town has seen in a month of miserable ones.

I'll confess something, since the page is otherwise so bare — a day like this always sets me thinking of the old crowd. Fifty years gone now since the last honest, flesh-and-blood folk of Gasket packed their wagons and rode for quieter country, leaving this dust-bowl to the rattling rabble that stayed behind. I like to imagine they'd have liked a day like today. Quiet. My joints did not even ache from the strain of writing about violence, which — between you and me — has been happening more than a upstanding man of my constitution ought to bear.

So enjoy it while it lasts, Gasket. Rest easy, oil your hinges if you've got 'em (I do not, being flesh, whatever the doctors keep muttering), and let tomorrow's ladder stay just as still as today's. A Sheriff can dream.
